concepts.name: Mission, vision and goals
concepts.summary: Define mission, vision and strategic objectives and recall how they guide strategic choices.

concepts.name: Strategy versus operations
concepts.summary: Explain that strategy is about choosing where to compete and how to win, distinct from running day-to-day activities efficiently.

concepts.name: Competitive advantage
concepts.summary: Explain competitive advantage as performing better than rivals in a way that yields higher returns than the industry average.

concepts.name: Target customers and value proposition
concepts.summary: Describe how a firm chooses which customers to serve and what value it offers them.

concepts.name: Cost leadership and differentiation
concepts.summary: Describe how a firm can win by lower cost or by offering distinctive value customers will pay more for.

concepts.name: Internal versus external environment
concepts.summary: Distinguish factors a firm controls from industry and macro forces it must respond to.

concepts.name: SWOT analysis
concepts.summary: Classify internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats for a company.

misconceptions.text: Strategy is just a detailed plan or budget for the next year.
Being the best at operational efficiency is the same as having a strategy.
A SWOT list on its own tells a firm what strategy to pursue.

concepts.name: PESTEL macro-environment scan
concepts.summary: Apply the political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal framework to identify external trends affecting a firm.

concepts.name: Porter's Five Forces
concepts.summary: Apply the five forces to assess how rivalry, entry, substitutes and supplier and buyer power shape industry profitability.

concepts.name: Value chain activities
concepts.summary: Map a firm's primary and support activities to locate where it creates cost or differentiation advantages.

concepts.name: Resources and capabilities
concepts.summary: Distinguish tangible and intangible resources from capabilities and relate them to advantage.

concepts.name: Competitor profiling
concepts.summary: Build a profile of rivals' offerings, strategies, strengths and likely moves.

concepts.name: Growth matrix options
concepts.summary: Use market penetration, market development, product development and diversification to classify growth options.

concepts.name: Market segmentation and positioning
concepts.summary: Segment a market and position an offering distinctively for chosen segments.

misconceptions.text: The most attractive industries are simply those growing fastest.
Five Forces analyses a single company rather than an industry's structure.
Any valuable resource gives a lasting advantage.

concepts.name: VRIO resource assessment
concepts.summary: Analyse whether resources are valuable, rare, costly to imitate and organized to be exploited, to judge advantage durability.

concepts.name: Strategic groups and mobility barriers
concepts.summary: Analyse how firms cluster by strategy within an industry and what keeps them from moving between groups.

concepts.name: Business model analysis
concepts.summary: Break down how a firm creates, delivers and captures value, including revenue and cost structure.

concepts.name: Corporate versus business strategy
concepts.summary: Differentiate the choice of which businesses to be in from how each business competes.

concepts.name: Portfolio analysis
concepts.summary: Use portfolio tools to assess business units and allocate resources across them.

concepts.name: Vertical integration decisions
concepts.summary: Analyse when owning upstream or downstream activities creates value versus using the market, using transaction costs.

concepts.name: Industry life cycle implications
concepts.summary: Analyse how competitive dynamics and strategic priorities shift across introduction, growth, maturity and decline.

concepts.name: Strategy and financial performance
concepts.summary: Link strategic position to profitability using margins, capital turnover and returns on invested capital.

misconceptions.text: A resource that is valuable and rare is automatically a sustained advantage.
The BCG matrix tells managers which units to keep or sell without further analysis.
Vertical integration always increases control and profit.

concepts.name: Game theory and competitive dynamics
concepts.summary: Analyse competitor moves and responses, such as price wars, signaling and commitment, as strategic games.

concepts.name: Dynamic capabilities
concepts.summary: Evaluate a firm's ability to sense change, seize opportunities and reconfigure resources in shifting markets.

concepts.name: Platforms and network effects
concepts.summary: Analyse how platform businesses gain advantage through network effects, multi-homing and switching costs.

concepts.name: Diversification and synergy evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether diversification creates value through shared resources, or destroys it through complexity and overpayment.

concepts.name: Mergers, alliances and acquisitions
concepts.summary: Evaluate build, buy and ally choices and the risks of integration and value capture.

concepts.name: Disruptive innovation dynamics
concepts.summary: Analyse how entrants with lower-end or new-market offerings displace incumbents and why incumbents struggle to respond.

concepts.name: International strategy choices
concepts.summary: Evaluate entry modes and the trade-off between global efficiency and local adaptation.

concepts.name: Strategic fit and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a firm's activities reinforce one another and make deliberate trade-offs that rivals cannot easily copy.

misconceptions.text: Synergies in acquisitions reliably materialize once the deal closes.
Disruptors win because their products are better than incumbents' from the start.
Network effects guarantee a winner-take-all outcome in any platform market.

concepts.name: Strategy formulation under uncertainty
concepts.summary: Design strategies that stay robust across plausible futures using scenarios and staged commitments.

concepts.name: Critiquing strategic frameworks
concepts.summary: Judge when frameworks such as Five Forces or the resource-based view mislead and which fits a given context.

concepts.name: Reshaping industry structure
concepts.summary: Create strategies that change industry boundaries or forces rather than just position within them.

concepts.name: Strategy execution and organization design
concepts.summary: Design structure, governance, metrics and incentives that turn strategic intent into consistent action.

concepts.name: Ecosystem and coopetition strategy
concepts.summary: Design positions within ecosystems and partnerships with rivals that capture value while sustaining partners.

concepts.name: Strategic renewal and turnaround
concepts.summary: Create plans to reinvent a firm's strategy or recover from decline while managing inertia and core rigidities.

concepts.name: Strategic decision biases
concepts.summary: Evaluate how overconfidence, anchoring and escalation distort strategic decisions and design safeguards.

misconceptions.text: Better analysis and forecasting remove the need to place strategic bets under uncertainty.
A sound strategy executes itself once it is announced.
Standard frameworks apply equally well to every industry and context.
